title: Ellington's works and tours from 1963: My People, Near East, Far East
summary: Dance prompts the 1963-64 tours and the Far East Suite.

blocks.x: Well, I wanted to ask you, before we get through, I just wanted to ask you which of his -- which of the Ellington things you really -- which ones were your favorites? So I want to just get back to that, Cootie, if you'd keep it in your mind. He did "My People" in 1963. I wanted to ask you what you feel about Jimmy Jones. He's a good musician, isn't he?
But he's a fine arranger and a --
I think he did "My People" for Duke. I think he did an awful lot of the scoring on it.

Or maybe mostly the conducting. I don't remember. But I remember he had quite a bit to do with it. In that same year, that was the first tour of the Near East and the Middle East. That must have been a little different experience.
Or was it still the same thing? Still a lot of concerts and a lot of audiences.
Okay. And the next year it was Japan, and Mercer had joined the band then. He joined as the band -- well, he played in a section, but he was the band manager, I guess, huh?
Right. Then he wrote the "Far East Suite", which was beautiful. "Mt. Harisa" and "Isfahan,"
Yeah. I remember all those things.
